entries.clue: Political defector: "Nicer, perhaps, being between two cards" (7)

indicatorNotes.perhaps: Perhaps says the word beside it is only one possible arrangement of its letters, not the one printed.
indicatorNotes.being between: Being between two things puts you in the middle of them, so the letters land inside the pair named.

blocks.note: the jack and the king, J and K on the pack, parting to let something in between them
the five letters of nicer in another order

annotation.surface: Someone quoted calling a turncoat the nicer one to be found between two playing cards.
annotation.walkthrough: Cards in a crossword are the court letters before they are anything else, and a jack and a king are all this one needs. The quotation marks hand the sneer to an unnamed colleague.
annotation.definitionFit: Robert Jenrick lost the Conservative whip and joined Reform UK on the same day in January 2026, so the surname alone serves as the political defector.

entries.clue: Shame bastards backed by state (6)

indicatorNotes.backed: Something backed comes at you the other way round, so those letters are entered in reverse.

blocks.note: gits is the British word for contemptible men, turned round
MA is Massachusetts as it is printed on an envelope

annotation.surface: Disgrace for some swine with a state behind them.
annotation.walkthrough: Git is a mild British insult for a worthless man, and it is the plural that gets turned. The state arrives as two letters rather than a name, which is the piece solvers hunt for last.
annotation.definitionFit: A stigma is the mark of disgrace that sticks to a person or a condition, which is shame made visible.

entries.clue: (&29dn.)Dot's loaded, having turned over a lot of money (4)

indicatorNotes.turned over: Turned over means flipped end for end, so the words it governs are read backwards.

blocks.note: a loaded lorry is a full one
pots of money is a lot of it, and the word is read the other way

annotation.surface: Dot turning out to be rich after cashing in a fortune.
annotation.walkthrough: Loaded is the money word the surface wants and the plain filled-to-the-brim word the wordplay wants. Pots for a large sum is everyday British: pots of cash, pots of it.
annotation.definitionFit: A full stop is the dot that ends a British sentence, the mark Americans call a period.

entries.clue: Settler welcomes Republican Hegseth's fake one? (6)

indicatorNotes.welcomes: To welcome someone is to take them in, so the letter named goes inside.

blocks.note: whoever settles the bill is the payer, and the word opens after its first letter
R is the letter printed after an American politician's name

annotation.surface: A homesteader making room for a Republican.
annotation.walkthrough: Settler is the trap: it looks like a pioneer on the frontier and means whoever picks up the bill. Pete Hegseth is Trump's defense secretary, and the Pentagon prayer services he stages are what the question mark is aimed at.
annotation.definitionFit: A prayer is what Hegseth performs in public, and the clue's verdict on that piety is what makes his a fake one.

entries.clue: (& 18dn.) Trump supporters beat up vegan meat mom (4)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is plural where the answer is a singular body: a movement is spoken of as the people in it, so the supporters and the thing they add up to are the same.

indicatorNotes.beat up: To beat something up is to knock it out of shape, and letters knocked out of shape do not stay in their printed order.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: Trump's followers laying into a mother who eats fake meat.
annotation.walkthrough: Beat up is the assault and the shuffling instruction in the same two words. MAGA is Make America Great Again, the slogan printed on the caps, and the movement is everyone wearing one.
annotation.definitionFit: The MAGA movement is the mass of Trump supporters gathered under his Make America Great Again slogan.

entries.clue: Joy's energy up with hair twisted and ring inserted (8)

indicatorNotes.twisted: A twisted thing has been wrung out of its proper shape, and so have the letters it is applied to.
indicatorNotes.inserted: What is inserted is pushed into the middle of something else, so that letter goes inside.

blocks.note: E is the physicist's symbol for energy
the little word itself, taken as its two letters
the four letters of hair in another order, parting to take a passenger
a ring is a circle, which is the shape of the letter O

annotation.surface: Joy's hair being put up, twisted and pinned with a ring.
annotation.walkthrough: Up is not an instruction here, only the word itself lying in the middle of the charade, which in a down entry is exactly where a turning instruction would sit. Joy is a name in the sentence and a plain noun in the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Euphoria is an intense, floating happiness, so joy names the same feeling at its strongest.

entries.clue: Crosses from bishop with elasticated opening on drawers (7)

indicatorNotes.opening: The opening of a word is where it starts, so only its first letter comes across.

blocks.note: B is the bishop on a chess scoresheet
the first letter of elasticated
the shallow sliding boxes in a chest are its trays

annotation.surface: Crucifixes from a bishop, and elastic-topped underwear, stowed in a chest.
annotation.walkthrough: Drawers is the joke: underpants in the sentence, the sliding boxes of a chest in the wordplay. Bishops supply B far more often than they supply crosses.
annotation.definitionFit: To cross somebody, in the double-crossing sense, is to betray them, and the plain verb carries that meaning without the double.

entries.clue: Earl joins a profiteer to go to The Ritz? (3,3)

blocks.note: E is the standard short form for earl
the article itself, taken as a letter
a tout buys tickets cheap and sells them dear outside the ground

annotation.surface: An earl teaming up with a ticket tout for dinner at a grand hotel.
annotation.walkthrough: The Ritz is the Piccadilly hotel whose dining room is the byword for expensive eating, so the question mark flags one example rather than a synonym. Earl is worth storing with the other peerage letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Going to The Ritz is one way of eating out, the definition naming a famous instance of the answer rather than a plain equivalent.

entries.clue: Darling's rate change, yes? (8)

indicatorNotes.change: A change leaves a thing no longer as it was, and that goes for the order of its letters.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 4 letters
sure is the casual yes, and its four letters join the shuffle

annotation.surface: Asking whether the Chancellor's move on interest rates is agreed.
annotation.walkthrough: Alistair Darling was Chancellor through the 2008 crash, so his name beside a rate change reads as Treasury news. The word wanted is the endearment, and the near-miss with his old department is deliberate.
annotation.definitionFit: Calling someone a treasure is calling them a darling: the noun you use of a person you prize.

entries.clue: Lustful? Immerse balls in crushed ice (6)

indicatorNotes.Immerse: To immerse a thing is to sink it right into whatever surrounds it.
indicatorNotes.in: In names the destination, so the letters just given go inside the ones that follow.
indicatorNotes.crushed: Crushed ice has been broken up and holds its shape no longer, and nor do the letters.

blocks.note: the three letters of ice in another order, parting to take a passenger
balls and rot are both dismissive words for nonsense

annotation.surface: Cooling a man's ardour by dropping his balls into crushed ice.
annotation.walkthrough: Balls is nonsense here, the way a load of rot is, and not the anatomy the sentence wants you picturing. The question mark admits the definition is loose in the direction it faces.
annotation.definitionFit: Erotic and lustful both belong to sexual desire, the answer describing what stirs it where the definition describes feeling it, which is the looseness the question mark concedes.

entries.clue: Loyal customer has bonk  gutted quite often (9)

indicatorNotes.gutted: A gutted thing has had its insides taken out, so the middle letter goes.

blocks.note: a regular is the customer who comes in every day
a bonk is a lay in the same slang sense, and that three-letter word has lost its middle

annotation.surface: A faithful customer whose sex life keeps being spoiled.
annotation.walkthrough: A regular is the drinker whose seat is always the same one, which is where the loyalty comes in. The definition hides in plain sight as the tail of the complaint.
annotation.definitionFit: Something done regularly happens at steady intervals, which in ordinary speech is quite often.

entries.clue: House caught between American-British hate (5)

indicatorNotes.caught between: Something caught between two things is trapped in the middle of them, so these letters go inside.

blocks.note: A is the short form for American and BR for British, run together as the hyphen suggests
Ho. is the short form for house on an address plate

annotation.surface: A house caught in the middle of a transatlantic quarrel.
annotation.walkthrough: Caught between promises a sandwich between the two nationalities; the house in fact lands inside the second of them, splitting the pair of letters that stands for British.
annotation.definitionFit: To abhor something is to hate it with revulsion, the strong end of the same verb.

entries.clue: Unrefined social group must change its direction (5)

indicatorNotes.must change its direction: Left and right are a single letter each in a crossword, so changing direction swaps one of those letters for the other.

blocks.note: a class is a social group, taken before anything happens to it

annotation.surface: A social group forced into a change of policy.
annotation.walkthrough: The word to find comes first and the alteration second, which is what makes a substitution slower than it looks. Only L and R are directions, and only one of them is in there.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone crass is coarse and tactless, unrefined in the sense of manners rather than of sugar.

entries.clue: Middle Eastern country's mood lifted with empty agreement (5)

indicatorNotes.lifted: Lifted means carried upwards, and in a down entry that is the direction these letters are read.
indicatorNotes.empty: An empty word keeps only its outer letters; everything between them has gone.

blocks.note: an air is the mood or atmosphere a place gives off
yes is the agreement, and emptying it leaves the Y and the S

annotation.surface: A country's spirits rising on a hollow deal.
annotation.walkthrough: It is the whole assembly that goes up, not one piece of it, so build the two chunks downwards and then read the column from the bottom. An air of menace is the sense of mood the wordplay wants.
annotation.definitionFit: Syria is a country on the eastern Mediterranean, so the definition names the region and the wordplay picks out the member.

entries.clue: Sadly, try to pray for politicians on the way out? (4,5)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is plural where the answer is a singular body, and it describes the members' prospects rather than giving a synonym; the question mark carries the paper's forecast.

indicatorNotes.Sadly: Sadly says the thing is in a sorry state, and letters in a sorry state have come out of their proper order.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Offering up a sad prayer for members whose careers are ending.
annotation.walkthrough: Praying for politicians on the way out reads as one whole thought, which is why the three words at the front are so hard to see as raw material. Jenrick's defection to Reform in January 2026 is the news behind the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The Tory Party is the Conservative Party, and the definition is the paper's verdict on where its politicians are heading.

entries.clue: City person Helen was quite taken by (5)

annotation.definition2: person Helen was quite taken by

blocks.note: the definition asks for a place, and the crossings decide which one

blocks.clueFragment: person Helen was quite taken by
blocks.note: the Trojan prince who carried Helen off from Sparta and started the war

annotation.surface: A city Helen rather fell for.
annotation.walkthrough: Taken by does both jobs at once: smitten with, in the sentence, and physically carried off, in the myth. Homer's prince and the French capital share five letters and nothing else.
annotation.definitionFit: Paris is the capital of France, and Paris was also the prince who took Helen from Sparta, so the same name answers to a city and to a person.

entries.clue: It's been perverted by Trump  "Liberal cameraman DIRE!" (8,5)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is a statement about the answer rather than a synonym for it: 'it' is the thing the clue says has been perverted, and the answer names that thing.

indicatorNotes.Liberal: Liberal means free and loose, and a liberal arrangement of letters is not the one printed.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: Trump shouting an insult at a news photographer.
annotation.walkthrough: Perverted sits exactly where a shuffling instruction usually sits and belongs instead to the definition. Counting settles it: cameraman and dire supply thirteen letters on their own, with no room for an L.
annotation.definitionFit: The American Dream is the promise that anyone in the States can rise by their own effort, and the clue says this presidency has made something else of it.

entries.clue: see 5dn.
Mark's about to enter without item of formal attire (6)

indicatorNotes.to enter: To enter something is to go inside it, so the letter named lands within the word that follows.

blocks.note: the item is a tie, and having none of one gives NO TIE, which opens before its last letter
c is short for circa, Latin for about

annotation.surface: A man on the point of walking into a formal do with no tie on.
annotation.walkthrough: Without does two jobs: it reads as lacking and it hands over the words themselves. Mark is the verb of mark my words, not the noun a tie-less guest would leave on the carpet.
annotation.definitionFit: To notice something is to mark it, the verb heard in mark my words and mark how he limps.

entries.clue: Complaint when Clare tears round House (7)

indicatorNotes.tears: Something torn has been pulled apart, and letters pulled apart go back in another order.
indicatorNotes.round: Going round a thing means passing all the way about it, so these letters end up on both sides of it.

blocks.note: the five letters of the name in another order, parting to take a passenger
Ho. is the short form for house on an address plate

annotation.surface: Clare rushing about the house in a temper.
annotation.walkthrough: Tears round reads as one phrase, somebody dashing about, and the wordplay needs it as two separate instructions. A complaint is an illness here rather than a grumble.
annotation.definitionFit: Cholera is a violent infection of the gut caught from dirty water, and complaint is the polite everyday word for an illness.

entries.clue: Crown, embarrassed to be caught by Cyclops had to get top people (2-5)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is plural where the answer is a collective singular: an in-crowd is nothing but the people in it.

indicatorNotes.embarrassed: Someone embarrassed is thrown into confusion, and letters thrown into confusion no longer stand where they did.
indicatorNotes.to be caught by: Being caught by somebody means ending up in their grasp, so these letters finish inside the ones named next.

blocks.note: Cyclops is the setter signing the puzzle, so he is I, and had supplies the 'd of I'd
the five letters of crown in another order

annotation.surface: The monarchy mortified at being nabbed by a one-eyed giant.
annotation.walkthrough: Setters put themselves into their own clues, and Cyclops as I is the convention at work here; had then supplies the apostrophe-d. The comma after Crown is punctuation for the sentence, not a break in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: The in-crowd is the fashionable set everyone else would like to be admitted to, which is what top people amounts to socially.

entries.clue: Try to engage in bestiality (4,1,2,2)

blocks.note: to try something is to attempt it
shift the last space one letter to the left and the same string describes a man and a farm animal

annotation.surface: An invitation to attempt something unspeakable with livestock.
annotation.walkthrough: The enumeration is the giveaway and the disguise at once: four little words, one of which can lend its opening letter to the next. Nothing is shuffled or hidden, and both halves are definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: To have a go at something is to try it, and re-spaced the same letters put a man in a field with a goat, which is the second definition's promise.

entries.clue: City's open source vote in favour of Democrat (6)

indicatorNotes.source: The source of a word is where it starts, so only its first letter comes across.

blocks.note: the first letter of open
a voter marks a cross in the box, and a cross is written X
to be in favour of something is to be for it, three letters as they stand
D is the letter printed after an American Democrat's name

annotation.surface: Open-source software throwing its weight behind a Democrat.
annotation.walkthrough: Open source is a computing phrase the eye reads as a single unit, and only the first letter of its first half is wanted. X is the mark a British voter puts in the box.
annotation.definitionFit: Oxford is a city in southern England, so the definition names the class and the wordplay picks out the member.

entries.clue: Alarm: sailor's downfall (5)

blocks.note: the wailing warning that goes off on an ambulance or a factory roof
in Homer, the singers on the rocks whose voices drew crews to their deaths

annotation.surface: An alarm that spells the end for a seaman.
annotation.walkthrough: The colon does all the joining, and both halves are definitions rather than wordplay. Odysseus had himself lashed to the mast so that he could hear the singing and live.
annotation.definitionFit: A siren is the wailing alarm of an emergency vehicle, and the Sirens of the Odyssey are the singers whose voices wrecked sailors on the rocks.

entries.clue: Lover's disgusting technique initially causes outrage (6)

indicatorNotes.disgusting: What disgusts you turns your stomach, and a turned thing does not come back in the order it went in.
indicatorNotes.initially: Initially asks for the initial, the single letter the word beside it begins with.

blocks.note: the five letters of lover in another order
the first letter of technique

annotation.surface: A lover's repellent bedroom technique scandalising somebody.
annotation.walkthrough: The shuffling instruction and the sentence's insult are the same word, which is why it never looks like an instruction. Outrage is a verb here, the thing done to somebody, not the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: To revolt someone and to outrage them are the same act: offending them past what they can stomach.

entries.clue: Politicians briefly grabbing male members (5)

indicatorNotes.briefly: Briefly asks for the short form of the word beside it rather than the whole of it.
indicatorNotes.grabbing: To grab something is to close your hand round it, so what is grabbed ends up inside.

blocks.note: the Liberals are the Libs in every headline, and the word parts to take a passenger
M is the box you tick for male on a form

annotation.surface: MPs having a quick grope.
annotation.walkthrough: Member is the pivot: a Member of Parliament in the sentence, and the old anatomical word for an arm or a leg in the definition. The crude reading in between is Cyclops's own.
annotation.definitionFit: A member of the body is a limb, the anatomical sense of the word, and both definition and answer are plural.

entries.clue: Seedy place? I say "Outstanding, on the up!" (4)

indicatorNotes.on the up: On the up means rising, and in a down entry rising letters are read from the bottom of the column.

blocks.note: oh! is the exclamation, the same noise as the British I say!
o/s is what an accountant writes against a bill still unpaid

annotation.surface: Somebody calling out that things are excellent and improving.
annotation.walkthrough: Outstanding means excellent in the quoted shout and unpaid in the wordplay, which is where its two letters come from. The whole assembly rises, so the column is read from the bottom.
annotation.definitionFit: Soho is the square mile of central London long known for its strip clubs and sex shops, which is the seediness the question mark points at.

entries.clue: Dial conservative type that's desperately needed by Trump? (4-5)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition describes what the answer would do for him rather than offering a synonym: the thing desperately needed is whatever lets him climb down without looking beaten.

blocks.note: dial is British slang for a face, as in shut your dial
someone conservative with money puts it away rather than spending it

annotation.surface: A cautious sort that the President urgently requires.
annotation.walkthrough: Conservative looks like the party and is the small-c habit with money, which is what makes the second half so hard to see. Dial for face is old British slang, still heard in shut your dial.
annotation.definitionFit: A face-saver is whatever lets someone retreat without looking beaten, which is what the clue says the President is short of.

entries.clue: see 3dn.
Become exhausted by Trots, Roth novel (3,5)

indicatorNotes.novel: Novel means new and unfamiliar, and an unfamiliar arrangement of the letters is what is asked for.

blocks.note: the trots and the runs are both slang for diarrhoea
the four letters of the name in another order

annotation.surface: Being worn out by Trotskyists and a Philip Roth novel.
annotation.walkthrough: Novel is the instruction and Philip Roth wrote novels, which is the whole joke. The two chunks do not break where the answer does: the S closes the first piece and opens the second word.
annotation.definitionFit: To run short of something is to have nearly used it up, which is what a supply becoming exhausted has done.

entries.clue: Depressed, hard to be a supporter? F-off! (6)

indicatorNotes.F-off!: Told to eff off, the letter F leaves the word it was sitting in and the rest closes up.

blocks.note: H is the hard grade stamped on a pencil
to follow somebody is to be a supporter of theirs, and the F has been sent packing

annotation.surface: A gloomy man told where to go for backing someone.
annotation.walkthrough: Depressed is the shape of a dent rather than a state of mind, which is the whole misdirection. The rude dismissal at the end is the instruction, and it names the letter that goes.
annotation.definitionFit: A hollow cheek or a hollow in a field is sunk below the level around it, which is depressed in the physical sense.
